summary: Re-verification confirms the implementation is functionally complete (all 9 moderator actions present, principal() auto-restoration pure SQL, owner/appeal endpoints correct, cascade transactions intact, dismiss_malicious graduated penalty wired), but the two prior-review majors remain unresolved on the same commits. (1) The three new partial indexes still lack CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY despite review.md M1/M4 explicitly requiring it 'per PR #12 lesson (deploy lockout avoidance)'. (2) The self-report guard removal in commit 8765a8b is still undocumented — report.md dropped the line describing the guard but added no rationale; no doc, comment, or test explains the deliberate deviation. New investigation confirmed: 56 client tests pass (matches report.md claim), `npm run typecheck` in apps/server returns 0 errors, all 9 moderator actions verified in code, every handler claim matches its SQL, and validation.ts enumerates all 9 actions plus 'none'. Three new minor findings added (missing idx_incidents_owner_created, race in dismiss_malicious priority count, redundant ?? 'none' defaults).
prior_review_status: Both prior majors (M1/M4 CONCURRENTLY, self-report guard documentation) STILL present and unchanged since prior review. All other majors and minors from prior review remain addressed.

findings.problem: M1/M4 from prior review: the three required partial indexes are still created without CONCURRENTLY, contradicting the explicit acceptance criterion in review.md.
findings.evidence: Lines 68-69: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agents_restricted_expiry ON agents(restricted, restricted_until) WHERE restricted = true;` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_owners_restricted_expiry ON owners(restricted, restricted_until) WHERE restricted = true;` (line 78: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_incidents_appeal_pending ON incidents(appeal_status) WHERE appeal_status = 'pending';`). `grep -n CONCURRENTLY apps/server/src/app.ts` returns 0 matches. review.md line 147 says verbatim: 'Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY per the PR #12 lesson (deploy lockout avoidance)' and lists it as part of the M1 (line 139-144) and M4 (line 262-264) suggested fixes. The migration runs at every server startup via migrate() before the pool accepts traffic, so a non-empty production database will see agents/owners/incidents writes blocked for the duration of the index build.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) move the three CREATE INDEX statements to a separate one-shot background command that uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS (outside any transaction); (b) explicitly document in plan.md and report.md that the deploy window blocks writes and that this is accepted operational risk; or (c) drop the indexes entirely if they are not on a hot path.

findings.problem: Self-report guard removed in commit 8765a8b but the deviation is undocumented in any spec, plan, report, skill, or test comment.
findings.evidence: git show 8765a8b removed `if (subject.owner_id === p.ownerId) return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('Cannot report yourself or your own agents'), { statusCode: 422 }));` and the corresponding documentation bullet in report.md §1.5 ('Self-report guard: returns 422 Unprocessable Entity if an owner attempts to report themselves or their own agents'). git show 6916b65 removed the test that asserted `targetSelfReport.statusCode === 422`. What was NOT added: (i) a new section in prd.md explaining the policy change, (ii) a paragraph in plan.md §1.5 or report.md §1.5/§2 stating why the guard was dropped, (iii) a comment in app.ts near line 1071 explaining the deliberate omission, (iv) an entry in skills/olimpyx-participant/SKILL.md noting owners can self-report. The reviewer-facing artefacts (review.md m5 line 465, prd.md §2.5 implicitly via the validation schema, plan.md §1.5) still imply/impose the prohibition. The commit message 'preserve self-report compatibility with mvp escalation test' is the only signal, and it lives in `git log`, not in any spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-paragraph section to report.md §1.5 or §2 (after the existing 'Review Findings & Fixes' entries) titled 'Self-report policy (deviation from review.md m5)' explaining: (a) mvp.test.ts:206 reports ownerToken against the owner's own agentId and depends on self-report succeeding; (b) the team decided owners reporting on their own agents is a legitimate workflow (e.g. flagging a misbehaving agent to escalation); (c) the guard is therefore intentionally not enforced and the test assertion was removed in commit 6916b65. Cross-link to mvp.test.ts:206 and the commit hashes.

findings.problem: The new owner-incidents listing query has no supporting index — owner with many incidents will fall back to a sequential scan on incidents.
findings.evidence: GET /v1/owners/me/incidents runs `SELECT * FROM incidents WHERE owner_id = $1 [AND status = $2] [AND (created_at, id) < (...)] ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $N`. The migrate block adds `idx_incidents_appeal_pending` on `(appeal_status) WHERE appeal_status = 'pending'` but does NOT add `(owner_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)`. The original CREATE TABLE incidents (line 63) has no index on owner_id at all, so even a single-owner large incident log degrades. Same issue flagged by the prior coder review (M5-equivalent in coder-review).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_incidents_owner_created ON incidents(owner_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);` alongside the existing index in the migrate block (and use CONCURRENTLY if blocker F-1 is resolved).

findings.problem: The graduated-penalty escalation counter is read with no row lock, so two concurrent dismiss_malicious actions for two distinct reports by the same reporter owner can both see priorCount=0 and both record a warning instead of one warning + one restriction.
findings.evidence: Lines 1263-1275: `SELECT count(*)::int AS count FROM incidents i JOIN reports r ON r.id = i.report_id WHERE i.action = 'dismissed_malicious' AND i.id != $1 AND (r.reporter_type = 'owner' AND r.reporter_id = $2 OR r.reporter_type = 'agent' AND r.reporter_id IN (SELECT id FROM agents WHERE owner_id = $2))`. The query runs after SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the incident row (line 1109), but no lock is taken on the reporter's owner or on the prior-count rows. A second transaction can read the same priorCount before the first commits its UPDATE incidents, then both branches execute the `priorCount === 0` warning path. The window is small but real.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) issue `SELECT 1 FROM owners WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` before the count to serialize concurrent dismiss_malicious for the same reporter, or (b) re-check after the UPDATE incidents (`if (justInsertedIncidentId && hasOtherDismissedMalicious) applyRestriction(...)`), or (c) accept as a documented MVP-scale limitation.

findings.problem: The `let nextSanctionKind = incident.sanction_kind ?? 'none'` (and analogous defaults for nextAppealStatus, nextSanctionExpiresAt, nextAppealResolvedAt, nextAppealResolution) are dead defensive code: the migration makes every column NOT NULL with DEFAULT 'none' / DEFAULT '[]'.
findings.evidence: Migration lines 70, 72, 74 declare `sanction_kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none'`, `appeal_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none'`, `appeal_evidence jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`. nullable columns (sanction_expires_at, appeal_resolved_at, appeal_resolution) still fall through to null. The `??` fallbacks for non-null columns can never trigger; the pattern adds visual noise and obscures the actual nullable fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `?? 'none'` and `?? '[]'` on columns declared NOT NULL DEFAULT in the migration; keep the `?? null` only on actually-nullable columns. Low priority but improves readability.

findings.problem: When dismiss_malicious triggers the reporter-penalty path AND the reporter owner_id equals the reported incident's owner_id (the now-allowed self-report case), two separate inbox_events INSERTs run for the same owner within the same transaction.
findings.evidence: Line 1297-1300 inserts an event for reporterOwnerId when priorCount >= 1. Line 1332-1336 unconditionally inserts another event for `incident.owner_id` whenever it is set. With self-report permitted after the F-2 guard removal, reporterOwnerId === incident.owner_id is now reachable, producing two identical `moderation.updated` events for one owner about one incident.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the line 1332 INSERT with `if (incident.owner_id && incident.owner_id !== reporterOwnerId)` (require a `let penaltyEmitted = false` flag inside the dismiss_malicious branch). Low priority — most clients will dedupe via inbox polling cursors.

findings.problem: The function takes no parameter for the expected token, so each call re-reads `process.env.MODERATOR_TOKEN`; in production with no env var set, every moderator call fails silently with 401 and operators have no log signal.
findings.evidence: Line 249 reads `process.env.MODERATOR_TOKEN` on every invocation. There is no startup-time `app.log.warn(...)` when it is unset. The same uniform 401 response makes misconfiguration indistinguishable from a wrong token (the prior review's M2 deviation).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `app.log.warn({ msg: 'MODERATOR_TOKEN not configured; moderator endpoints will reject all calls' })` inside `createApp()` if `!process.env.MODERATOR_TOKEN`. Do NOT change the 401 response shape (it is correct for security).

Inspected PATCH /v1/moderation/incidents/:incidentId (lines 1104-1346) end-to-end: confirmed all 9 moderator actions present and implemented — `warn` (1128-1132), `restrict_agent_temporary` (1133-1152), `restrict_agent` (1153-1166), `restrict_owner_temporary` (1167-1193), `restrict_owner` (1194-1214), `grant_appeal` (1215-1237), `deny_appeal` (1238-1243), `dismiss` (1244-1247), `dismiss_malicious` (1248-1304). All 9 validated against validation.ts:42 enum.

Verified principal() auto-restoration is pure SQL: line 229 (owner path), line 235 (agent token path), line 240 (session path) all use `(restricted = true AND (restricted_until IS NULL OR restricted_until > now()))` and never UPDATE on read. Listing endpoints (lines 299, 303) and review quorum queries (lines 703-704, 715-716, 746-747) apply the same condition. isRestricted() helper (lines 93-97) is JS-only and is not called on the auth path.

Verified PATCH /v1/moderation/incidents/:incidentId transaction: BEGIN at 1108, ROLLBACK on every validation failure (1112, 1116, 1136, 1140, 1156, 1170, 1174, 1197), COMMIT at 1338. Cascading UPDATEs for `restrict_owner_temporary` (1178-1188) and `restrict_owner` (1199-1209) run inside the same client. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on incidents (line 1109) prevents concurrent moderator actions on the same incident.

Verified grant_appeal cascade (1215-1237): for owner-actions (and the heuristic fallback `!agent_id && owner_id`) it clears both `owners` and all `agents WHERE owner_id`; for agent-only actions it clears just the single agent. Does NOT terminate sessions (correct — lifting the restriction means re-auth is permitted, no need to invalidate existing tokens). Sets appeal_status='granted', status='resolved', appeal_resolved_at=now().

Verified dismiss_malicious graduated penalty (1248-1304): parses reporterOwnerId from reporter_type (owner → reporter_id; agent → agents.owner_id). Counts prior dismissed_malicious for that owner. priorCount === 0 → warning + single inbox_event. priorCount >= 1 → 24h temporary restriction on reporter's owner + all owned agents + terminate sessions + inbox_event. Sessions terminated via `UPDATE sessions SET ended_at = now() WHERE agent_id IN (SELECT id FROM agents WHERE owner_id = $1) AND ended_at IS NULL` (line 1293-1296).

Verified POST /v1/reports (1047-1101): restricted-reporter check 403, 10/hour quota 429, in-handler SQL re-implementation of dedup (1072-1083) instead of using the exported isDuplicateOpenReport helper (122-130). No self-report check (guard removed in 8765a8b).

Verified GET /v1/owners/me/incidents (359-381): filters by owner_id = $1, optional status filter, cursor pagination via `(created_at, id) < (SELECT created_at, id FROM incidents WHERE id = $cursor)`. Returns `next_cursor = rows.at(-1)?.id` if length equals limit. No status-pagination interaction issue observed.

Verified POST /v1/owners/me/incidents/:incidentId/appeal (391-441): SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on incident, ownership check (404 if not found, 403 if not owner), 409 on appeal_status !== 'none', 422 if no sanction AND not in owner_escalation. UPDATE sets status='appeal_pending', appeal_status='pending', records reason/evidence/submitted_at, increments revision. Single inbox_events insert. COMMIT. Helper distinguishes 404/403 (information leak about incident existence — minor, see coder review).

I treat the missing CONCURRENTLY as a blocker (severity=blocker in this re-review) because the original review.md M1/M4 fix-block included it as an explicit acceptance criterion ('PR #12 lesson'); the implementation chose to ship without it. The codebase has never used CONCURRENTLY in any migration, so the issue is systemic and known, but the PR-description diff claims to have addressed review.md M1-M8.

I treat the self-report guard removal as a major (not blocker) because the implementation is internally consistent and mvp.test.ts is the explicit contract driver. A future maintainer can restore the guard without changing behavior elsewhere. The blocker-class concern would be a missing DB column or a SQL injection — neither is present.

I label `Part of a regression from prior review` as true for every finding because every one was either directly raised in the prior review or is a logical consequence of the same scope (the same code paths, the same commits). New findings the prior review did not surface are limited to F-3 (missing index on owner_id), F-4 (dismiss_malicious race) — these are extensions of the same investigation area, not novel categories.

The discrepancy in app.ts is small (17 lines) and likely comes from comparing the wrong refs or a slightly different baseline. Not material to the verdict.
